idiom_name: module-private type whose whole interface is primitives and its own type
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: express the type's complete public surface in primitives, standard-library types and its own type; move every helper that would need the surrounding model out of the class and into the caller or a service; then close the boundary with the strongest mechanism the language offers (private members, package or module visibility, file-private helpers, an opaque handle) so the isolation is enforceable rather than aspirational. Operations should take and return the type itself so clients compose instances without importing the model. Persistence, serialization and framework integration belong in a separate mapper, never in the class.
code_sketch:
type Money = (amount: exact decimal, currency: code)   // primitives only
    plus(Money) -> Money                                // closure of operations
    times(decimal) -> Money
    never imports Customer, Order, Repository           // no model references
boundary: private members | package/module privacy | opaque handle
pitfalls: Leaving one convenience method that walks into the model re-establishes exactly the coupling the pattern removes.
Splitting the class's invariants between the class and its callers: each piece looks simple and the combination is wrong.
Making the boundary a naming convention only - the next contributor will not notice it, and no tool will complain.

Wrong move: keeping the ORM/JPA annotation or framework base class on the class because mapping lives there -> the class now imports the framework, every reader needs the framework manual, and unit tests boot the persistence stack -> map it from a separate Data Mapper or persistence entity instead.

Wrong move: accepting a neighbour's type as a parameter 'just to read one field' -> the neighbour's semantics ride into every call site and the one-line fixture stops compiling -> pass the needed field as a primitive and let the caller do the lookup.

Wrong move: deleting genuine behaviour from the class to keep the dependency count at zero -> the type decays into getters and setters while a service accumulates the rules (Fowler's Anemic Domain Model) -> keep the behaviour and let the collaborator's knowledge arrive as data or as an injected primitive-returning function at the composition root.
